findings.reason: the first Deliverable item and its first test rest on a mechanism the section's own measurement contradicts, so a node would build a cache that cannot reduce the object accumulation and read its passing test as having fixed the Why.
findings.text: The Why attributes the 7,692 loose objects (about 95% trees) to conflict checks that run "every pass, each check writes the merged tree"; the section's new sentence now states that repeating a merge over identical inputs writes no new object, and I measured that this holds (two consecutive `git merge-tree --write-tree` runs over the same base and head in a temporary repository left the loose count unchanged at 10; a conflicting pair stayed at 18), so an already-checked (primary revision, head) pair writes nothing at all on any later check, and the trees must come from pairs that were never checked before (a moved primary or a new candidate head) — exactly the pairs a cache "for a primary revision and head already checked" cannot answer from an earlier result — while the same wrong mechanism is written into the open followup f-wftl-028 ("conflict checks stop writing a new tree on every pass")

findings.reason: the section would be split into two nodes, each closable on its own verdict, rather than one 1.5-hour node whose gate fails for either half.
findings.text: §65 mixes two deliverables with separate failure modes and separate tests: answering an existing conflict check from its earlier result in the landing path, and building a scheduled maintenance pass (packing, cruft retention, `gc.log` clearing, a before/after record surfaced in the crew view, and submission by the fleet's long-running service), which no single gate verdict can close or refuse as one node

response_events.note: §65 no longer caches a check's result; its endpoint is that a conflict check leaves no object in the repository, tested with the primary advancing between passes, which is where the loose trees come from

reasoning-1.note: §65 no longer caches a check's result; its endpoint is that a conflict check leaves no object in the repository, tested with the primary advancing between passes, which is where the loose trees come from

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — §65 cites no href; the one reference that could fail to resolve, f-wftl-028 (plan.html:486), exists, is `open`, and its prompt names §65 as the same section it describes.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — the changed first case measures the endpoint that actually distinguishes a cached answer (the second pass runs no merge-tree computation) rather than a count that cannot move, and its declared negative control names the same observable on the same case; the second and third cases read the crew view's recorded loose count, the removal of a placed stale `gc.log`, and the submitted job's partition, so none of them is satisfied by the base revision.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate log and the live run's before/after counts go to the section's evidence fragment after landing, not a scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the section names mechanisms (`git merge-tree --write-tree`, cruft packs, `gc.log`) and carries no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags into anything a node would create.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the Why's explanation of how the loose trees accumulated is contradicted by the section's own new done-when sentence and by measurement: a repeated check over identical inputs writes no object, so repeated conflict checks cannot be what wrote 2,345 trees in a day.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §65 carries two independently reviewable deliverables, a conflict-check result cache in the landing path and a scheduled maintenance pass with its record, crew view and service submission.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §65 declares no depends-on/gates, section s65 is declared `implementable` in plan-section-declarations, and the one open followup for it (f-wftl-028, plan.html:486) names `/reckon-build work-flows-to-the-lane §65`, so a coordinator driving open followups dispatches the section once.
